newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine gov't to meet YPF over oil spill.
newsitem.headline: Argentine gov't to meet YPF over oil spill.

text.p: Argentine Energy Secretary Alfredo Mirkin will fly to an oil spill site to inspect damage and meet officials of oil firm YPF, which is defying an order to shut wells, his office said Friday.
Mirkin's spokesman Carlos Serrano said that an administrative complaint YPF lodged with the government Thursday would not affect the order to close the wells.
"In no way does it get in the way of the order to close the wells totally and temporarily," Serrano said.

YPF lodged an official challenge to the Energy Secretariat's order to close 112 wells in the provinces of Neuquen and Mendoza due to oil leaks from pipelines into the 600-mile (1,000 km) long Colorado River.
Serrano said reports that thousands of cubic meters had split into the Colorado appeared to be false, but that Mirkin would travel to inspect personally the environmental damage.

"We don't know exactly how many cubic meters (of oil were spilt), but we know it is not as much as the press has been seeing over the past few days," he said. "But anyway, if the spilt oil has polluted the drinking water supply then that justifies the (order to close the wells)."
The Colorado is the water supply for the Neuquen town of Rincon de los Sauces, and the local municipality has distributed mineral water for the people to drink.

Local newspapers published pictures of the river smothered by a muddy cap of oil and Neuquen's Water and Health Office director charged YPF's pipelines were poorly built in violation of international norms.
YPF took out a paid advertisement in Argentine newspapers Thursday declaring it would close just 59 wells, affecting a tiny part of its production in the area.
Admitting it had split 25 cubic meters of oil into the Colorado after wild storms damaged pipelines, it said there was no technical reason to close any more wells.
The company said that the spillage was an unforeseeable result of freakish weather.
Serrano said Friday the company appeared to be giving in and closing the wells it was told to.
"Apparently, YPF is obeying the Secretariat's resolution," Serrano said.
But a YPF spokeswoman contradicted him, saying the company was holding firm to the position it declared Thursday.
"That is the situation and the situation has not changed," a YPF spokeswoman told Reuters.
She said Mirkin would meet YPF's vice-President for Upstream Marcelo Guiscardo in Rincon de los Sauces next week.
YPF is Argentina's largest listed company.
